title: Hybrid eval cost-fidelity splitter and routing framework
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This document defines the "Hybrid Eval Cost-Fidelity Splitter" (HECFS) — a deterministic policy and runtime component that routes evaluation probes across multiple fidelity tiers (smoke, standard, deep) to maximize coverage and failure signal while enforcing a configurable cost budget. HECFS provides (1) an allocation algorithm, (2) runtime routing knobs, (3) operational SLOs/metrics, and (4) a small runbook for triage when the splitter misbehaves.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineers operating the eval harness and shadow fleets
- Platform engineers integrating probe routing into shadow and federated evaluators
- Product owners responsible for evaluation cost/perf tradeoffs

Why this exists:
- Continuous evaluation at scale has variable marginal value: not every probe needs full-fidelity instrumentation.
- Without systematic allocation, teams either overspend on deep evaluation or under-detect regressions.
- HECFS provides a principled way to amortize eval spend while preserving sensitivity to regressions.

Scope and definitions:
- Probe: a single evaluation input (prompt + metadata) executed by the harness.
- Fidelity tiers:
  - smoke: single seed, lightweight metrics, fast, lowest cost.
  - standard: deterministic seed set, additional metrics (coherence, hallucination proxies).
  - deep: multi-seed, function-call simulation, quant-shadow comparison, human review gating.
- Cost unit: normalized token-cost equivalent (used by the budget allocator).
- Sensitivity score: dynamic estimate of how likely a probe is to reveal a regression (0.0–1.0).

High-level design:
1) Offline profiling produces per-slice base-cost and baseline-variance. Profiling includes quant-shadow runs and prefix-cache sensitivity.
2) A lightweight estimator assigns each incoming probe a sensitivity score s and an expected token_cost c for each fidelity tier.
3) The Splitter uses a knapsack-inspired allocator to distribute probes into fidelity buckets given the global budget B and soft quality target Q (target detection probability).
4) A small rebalancer runs every minute to migrate probes (where possible) from standard -> deep or deep -> standard based on live telemetry (e.g., rising variance, new latency anomalies).
5) Routing decisions are recorded in the probe registry and emitted as telemetry (route_reason, expected_cost, chosen_tier, estimator_version).

Allocation policy (concise):
- Prioritize high-sensitivity probes for deep evaluation until marginal detection gain < marginal cost fraction.
- Maintain a minimum coverage floor: at least X% of probes in each important slice must be run at standard fidelity to preserve baseline comparability.
- Reserve a small opportunistic budget P for on-demand deep escalations triggered by anomaly detectors.

Configuration table (example):
| parameter | meaning | recommended default | notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| global_budget_B | total token-cost budget per-hour for eval fleet | 15_000_000 | set at account/team level |
| quality_target_Q | target detection probability (0-1) | 0.92 | soft target used by allocator |
| floor_coverage_slice | min percent of probes per slice at standard | 0.10 | important slices set by ownership |
| opportunistic_reserve_P | percent of B reserved for escalations | 0.06 | used for anomaly-driven deep runs |
| estimator_version | model id used to compute sensitivity | v2025-11-17 | pinned per-deployment |

Estimator notes:
- The estimator uses a small ensemble: a lightweight classifier over probe metadata + recent telemetry (token length, tenant, historical failure rate) and an uncertainty proxy (variance estimate from prior seeds).
- Estimator must be validated offline against prior incidents (see validation checklist below).

Pseudocode: allocation loop

# Inputs: probes[], B, Q, floor_coverage, P
# Outputs: routing decisions {probe_id -> tier}

1. sort probes by sensitivity_score descending
2. allocate_reserved = B * P
3. remaining_budget = B - allocate_reserved
4. ensure per-slice floor: for each slice s, mark floor_count(s) = max(floor_coverage * count(s), 1) and allocate those at standard tier, deducting expected cost
5. for probe in probes (high -> low sensitivity):
     expected_deep_cost = cost(probe, deep)
     marginal_gain = marginal_detection_gain(probe, deep vs standard)
     if remaining_budget >= expected_deep_cost and marginal_gain / expected_deep_cost >= threshold(Q):
         assign probe -> deep; remaining_budget -= expected_deep_cost
     else if remaining_budget >= cost(probe, standard):
         assign probe -> standard; remaining_budget -= cost(probe, standard)
     else:
         assign probe -> smoke
6. opportunistic pool: route up to allocate_reserved probes to deep when anomaly detectors flag them

Operational metrics (emitted every minute and available in Console dashboards):
- route_distribution: pct {smoke, standard, deep} (goal: stable within 5% of configured target)
- budget_utilization: used_B / B (alert at > 0.95)
- detection_gain_curve: marginal_detection_vs_cost (visualization to tune threshold)
- false_negative_rate_estimate (post-hoc labeling pipeline)
- escalations: count of opportunistic_reserve usages (alert if > configured P limit)
- estimator_drift_index: KL divergence of estimator feature distribution vs training baseline

SLOs and thresholds:
- Evaluator sensitivity SLO: maintain estimated detection probability >= Q - 0.03 (soft).
- Budget SLO: no more than 1% of hours with budget_utilization > 1.0 (hard).
- Escalation SLO: opportunistic_reserve usage limited to configured P within a 24h window.

Rollout plan (canary -> graduated):
1. Canary (5% of eval fleet across low-risk tenants): run HECFS in audit mode (make routing decisions but do not enforce; log "shadow_route" field) for 48-72 hours. Compare budget/utilization predictions and detection_gain_curve vs baseline.
2. Soft-enforce (25%): enforce routing, but keep a doubled opportunistic_reserve to allow manual escalations. Run human-in-loop reviews for any missed high-sensitivity probes.
3. Enforce (all): full policy, enable automated rebalancer.

Promotion checklist (must pass before increasing traffic fraction):
- estimator false positive/negative rates on canary labels < 10%
- budget_utilization predictions within 8% of observed
- detection_gain_curve monotonic (no counter-intuitive inversions)
- monitoring dashboards verified and alerting wired to oncall

Failure modes and runbook (top 5):
1) Overbudget (budget_utilization > 1.0)
   - Immediate action: toggle global_budget_B to emergency-reduced value (CLI: hecfs-cli set-budget --id <env> --value <reduced_B>) and scale opportunistic_reserve_P to 0
   - Triage: check estimator version, recent traffic spike, and any new slices with unexpectedly high deep_cost
   - Postmortem: corrective action may include increasing economy of standard tier or adjusting floor_coverage_slice

2) Estimator drift (estimator_drift_index > drift_threshold):
   - Action: revert to fallback_estimator (rule-based) and open ticket for retraining.

3) Detection regression (false_negative_rate_estimate increases > baseline + 0.05):
   - Action: pause deep -> standard demotions, temporarily promote top N high-sensitivity probes to deep for human review.

4) Router lag (routing decisions delayed > 2s):
   - Action: switch to stateless fallback routing (round-robin based on slice priority) and scale routing workers.

5) Telemetry loss: missing route_reason or chosen_tier fields
   - Action: pause enforcement, enable audit-only mode until telemetry pipeline repaired.

Validation and bench tests (recommended suites):
- Synthetic spike test: create a burst of high-sensitivity probes in a low-budget simulation and assert opportunistic_reserve limits are respected.
- Regression injection: replay a historic incident (known regression) and verify detection probability under HECFS >= baseline detection.
- Cost simulation sweep: run iterated allocators across B values to produce detection_vs_cost frontier for stakeholders.

Interfaces and example CLI commands:
- hecfs-cli evaluate-batch --input probes.json --budget 15000000 --estimator v2025-11-17 --output routing.csv
- hecfs-cli set-budget --env staging --value 10000000
- hecfs-cli promote-estimator --env prod --version v2026-01-12 --rollback-to v2025-11-17

Telemetry schema (fields emitted per probe):
- probe_id (string)
- tenant_id (string)
- slice_id (string)
- sensitivity_score (float)
- chosen_tier (string)
- expected_cost_per_tier (string; comma-separated cost map)
- route_reason (string)
- estimator_version (string)

Ownership and escalation contacts:
- Primary owner: Maya Chen (Applied ML Platform) — pager: #applied-ml-oncall

Documentation and developer guidance:
- How to run local allocator: repo: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-splitter (README has docker dev image and test harness)
- Unit tests required: allocator unit tests, estimator regression test, cost-sensitivity integration suite (CI gate)

Appendix A: Estimator validation checklist
- Holdout dataset: at least 10K labeled probes spanning longtail slices
- Minimum AUC: 0.78 for high vs low sensitivity classification
- Calibration curve: max ECE < 0.07
- Adversarial checks: vary tokenization and quantized model runs to ensure false negatives don't spike

Appendix B: Example allocation simulation table
| scenario | B | allocated_deep_pct | expected_detection | notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| baseline | 15_000_000 | 18% | 0.92 | uses default params |
| constrained-budget | 6_000_000 | 7% | 0.74 | triggers more smoke |
| high-reserve | 15_000_000 (P=0.2) | 25% | 0.95 | opportunistic finds rare regs |

Notes and open questions:
- Investigate whether tenant-prioritization should be a separate multiplier in the objective (fairness vs detection tradeoff).
- Explore adaptive floor_coverage per slice based on seasonal traffic patterns.
